title: Kapoora Refuses the Guru and Meets the Foretold Hanging

blocks.text: Kapoora explains his refusal in blunt political terms: we are servants of the Turks, and if he shelters the Guru in his fort the imperial authorities will destroy him. His speech shows a chief trying to preserve his worldly position by abandoning the higher obligation of hospitality and loyalty.

The Guru answers that such caution will not save him, because faithlessness itself has already chosen his ruin. The page frames the warning as a prophecy whose force is both temporal and spiritual, insisting that the Guru's word does not go in vain.

The narrative then moves toward fulfillment as Isa Khan Manjh enters the story and Kapoora's intrigues rebound against him. What he feared outwardly finally happens in fact, and Kapoora is hanged just as the Guru had foretold.
